title: Fill the Command Line
story: Real tools take options from the command line. Pretend the user typed --name Asha.
starter:
import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--name", default="world")
args = parser.parse_args(___)
print("Hello, " + args.name)
hints: parse_args takes a list of the words the user typed.

import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--name", default="world")
args = parser.parse_args(["--name", "Asha"])
print("Hello, " + args.name)
socratic: How would the user's typing look as a list?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what did the blank teach you in “Fill the Command Line”?
solution:
import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--name", default="world")
args = parser.parse_args(["--name", "Asha"])
print("Hello, " + args.name)
